annotation_policy: Provisional human labels from canonical portfolio metadata and visible browser frames. They test disciplined uncertainty: fields that require full playback stay unknown. Promote to gold only after two reviewers inspect the complete video and timestamp disagreements.

annotations.ui_usage: Expected central product evidence; full playback verification required
motion_patterns: unknown — do not infer from portfolio still
strengths: Portfolio framing ties the work to one named product update
weaknesses: Scene mechanics are not exposed by portfolio metadata
reusable_visual_principles: Anchor a feature launch around the changed capability rather than a general brand overview
risks_non_copy: Do not reuse Lovable's interface, brand language, colors, or launch sequence

weaknesses: Cannot separate brand craft from product explanation without playback
reusable_visual_principles: When brand and product change together, make the relationship explicit rather than alternating unrelated brand and UI scenes
risks_non_copy: Do not imitate the rebrand identity or reveal choreography

annotations.ui_usage: A visible inspected frame presents an assistant-style analysis result rather than a full dashboard
motion_patterns: unknown — video playback unavailable in inspection
strengths: Finding is readable as the focal point
weaknesses: A single frame cannot establish the complete narrative
reusable_visual_principles: For an analysis product, elevate the discovered finding above the surrounding interface chrome
risks_non_copy: Do not copy typography, monochrome treatment, wording, or exact centered layout

strengths: Candidate is relevant when explaining multimodal/video mechanisms
weaknesses: Only project title and type were available
reusable_visual_principles: Select references by matching the mechanism to explain, not merely the AI category
risks_non_copy: Do not treat a portfolio title as evidence of scene execution

composition_patterns: feature sequence around one product surface
annotations.ui_usage: Core evidence; portfolio copy names three visible product actions
motion_patterns: UI state changes expected; full playback verification required
weaknesses: Portfolio metadata does not reveal attention order
reusable_visual_principles: In a short feature launch, group actions around one persistent product surface
risks_non_copy: Do not copy Bolt's interface, wording, or feature order

annotations.hierarchy_focal_point: workflow moving from configuration to deployment
strengths: Portfolio description exposes a causal product sequence
reusable_visual_principles: Preserve the same workflow object across create, customize, and deploy states
risks_non_copy: Do not reuse Bleu AI's node design, palette, or exact sequence

annotations.ui_usage: Case study confirms storyboard in Figma and a feature-launch purpose; scene use requires playback
strengths: Feature and launch objective are explicit
weaknesses: Studio performance claims do not explain visual causality
reusable_visual_principles: Keep launch success metrics separate from evidence that a visual mechanism communicates clearly
risks_non_copy: Do not reuse ClickUp brand assets or treat claimed reach as transferable proof

weaknesses: Case study emphasizes reach more than scene mechanics
reusable_visual_principles: Evaluate the opening hook separately from the mechanism explanation and from distribution outcomes
risks_non_copy: Do not copy the hook, identity, sequence, or use view counts as causal evidence
